newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Woodchester says outlook favourable.
newsitem.headline: Woodchester says outlook favourable.

text.p: Irish-based financial services firm Woodchester Investments Plc said on Thursday the economic outlook in all its markets was favourable and the level of new business advances had grown strongly.
Woodchester said all divisions performed well during the first half of 1996.

"Good progress was made towards attaining the group's key objectives for 1996, namely the achievment of further growth in our businesses and the centralisation of many of our back office operations," Chairman Craig McKinney said in the company's interim results statement.
Woodchester reported a 25 percent jump in pre-tax profit to 21.42 million punts in the first six months of 1996.
The level of new business advances grew strongly and in the first half of 1996 total new business reached almost 600 million Irish pounds, an increase of 46 percent over the same period last year.
"A pleasing highlight since the half-year end was the attainment of a record level of new business advances in August amounting to 120 million Irish pounds," McKinney said.
He said a key strategic development was progress in centralisation of back office operations.

Business units and branches continue to be responsible for sales, marketing and underwriting in local markets but some of the groups's back office activities are being relocated on a phased basis to a central processing centre in Dublin.

McKinney said growth in new business and profits in Denmark and Portugal showed the two operations were reaching critical mass and could now be expected to make a meaningful contribution to group profitability.
"Following on from these successes, consideration is being given to the commencement of business in a further European country," he said.

The Denmark operation continued from "stength to strength", McKinney said, growing its portfolio to over 130 million punts from an original 20 million when Woodchester acquired it from Credit Lyonnais two years ago.
In Portugal the volume of new business advances increased by more than three times that of the year-ago period, he said.

In Ireland there was a significant rise in motor finance new business volumes, and a good start was made to new operations in Northern Ireland, Woodchester said. Motor finance in Britain also achieved good growth in new business volumes, it said.
Woodchester is majority-owned by Credit Lyonnais.
